      "unit": "F001:F004",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "definition",
        "scope_quotes": [],
        "scope_text": "",
        "context_quotes": [

        ],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",

        "logic_quote": "F001:F004",
        "references": [
          "§ 825.801",
          "§ 825.105(b)"
        ],
        "statement": "An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to § 825.801 for special hours of service requirements for airline flight crew employees), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) regarding employees working outside the U.S.)."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F005",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F005:F006"
        ],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, provided that employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted subject to the exceptions in paragraph (b)(2).",
        "context_quotes": [
          "F001:F002"
        ],
        "modality_quote": "need not",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F005",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted except as provided in paragraph (b)(2)."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F006",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F006"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of 29 CFR 825.110.",
        "context_quotes": [
          "F005"
        ],
        "modality_quote": "need not",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F006",
        "references": [
          "paragraph (b)(2)"
        ],
        "statement": "In determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F007:F009",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F007:F009"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Where the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her USERRA-covered service obligation, or where a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.",
        "context_quotes": [
          "F006"
        ],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [
          "F008",
          "F009"
        ],
        "choice_quote": "F007:F009",
        "choice_text": "Either the break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation, or a written agreement exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.",
        "logic_quote": "F007:F009",
        "references": [
          "USERRA",
          "38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq."
        ],
        "statement": "Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where either: (i) the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her USERRA (38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq.) covered service obligation; or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F008",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F007:F008"
        ],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, where there is absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F008",
        "references": [
          "USERRA",
          "38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq."
        ],
        "statement": "The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer; however, this section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under USERRA."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F010",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F010"
        ],
        "scope_text": "If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F010",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits, etc.), the week counts as a week of employment, and for purposes of determining whether intermittent/occasional/casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "permission",
        "scope_quotes": [],
        "scope_text": "",
        "context_quotes": [
          "F006"
        ],
        "modality_quote": "Nothing in this section prevents",
        "modality": "may",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F011",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Employers are permitted to consider employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F011"
        ],
        "scope_text": "If an employer chooses to recognize prior employment preceding a continuous break in service of more than seven years.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F011",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "If an employer chooses to recognize prior employment preceding a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly, with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F012"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 containing the special hours of service requirement for airline flight crew employees.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F012",
        "references": [
          "paragraph (c)(2)",
          "§ 825.801",
          "FLSA",
          "29 CFR part 785"
        ],
        "statement": "Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to the principles established under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) for determining compensable hours of work (see 29 CFR part 785); the determining factor is the number of hours worked for the employer within the meaning of the FLSA, which is not limited by methods of recordkeeping or inaccurate compensation agreements."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "permission",
        "scope_quotes": [],
        "scope_text": "",
        "context_quotes": [
          "F012"
        ],
        "modality_quote": "may",
        "modality": "may",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F012",
        "references": [
          "FLSA"
        ],
        "statement": "Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA's principles may be used to determine whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F013"
        ],
        "scope_text": "For an employee returning from or reemployed following USERRA-covered service, in determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave (subject to § 825.801(c) for airline flight crew employees).",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "shall",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F013",
        "references": [
          "USERRA",
          "§ 825.801(c)"
        ],
        "statement": "An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service in determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave, adding those hours to any hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period to meet the hours of service requirement (referencing § 825.801(c) for airline flight crew employees)."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F013"
        ],
        "scope_text": "In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "can generally",
        "modality": "possible",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F013",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, the employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F014",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F014"
        ],
        "scope_text": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including for employees who are exempt from FLSA's recordkeeping requirement under 29 CFR part 541.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "has the burden",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F014",
        "references": [
          "FLSA",
          "29 CFR part 541",
          "§ 825.102",
          "§ 825.801(d)"
        ],
        "statement": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including employees exempt from FLSA's recordkeeping requirement, the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours, and must be able to clearly demonstrate (for example, regarding full-time teachers) that the employee did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim the employee is not eligible for FMLA leave (referencing § 825.801(d) for airline flight crew employees)."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F015",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [],

        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F015",
        "references": [
          "§ 825.300(b)"
        ],
        "statement": "The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F015",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F015"
        ],
        "scope_text": "When an employee is on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "would be",

        "alternative_quotes": [],

      }

unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to § 825.801 for special hours of service requirements for airline flight crew employees), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) regarding employees working outside the U.S.).

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, provided that employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted subject to the exceptions in paragraph (b)(2).
unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted except as provided in paragraph (b)(2).

unit_attributes.scope_text: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of 29 CFR 825.110.
unit_attributes.statement: In determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Where the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her USERRA-covered service obligation, or where a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Either the break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation, or a written agreement exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.
unit_attributes.statement: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where either: (i) the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her USERRA (38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq.) covered service obligation; or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, where there is absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer; however, this section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under USERRA.

unit_attributes.scope_text: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits, etc.), the week counts as a week of employment, and for purposes of determining whether intermittent/occasional/casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months.
Employers are permitted to consider employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: If an employer chooses to recognize prior employment preceding a continuous break in service of more than seven years.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employer chooses to recognize prior employment preceding a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly, with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 containing the special hours of service requirement for airline flight crew employees.
unit_attributes.statement: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to the principles established under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) for determining compensable hours of work (see 29 CFR part 785); the determining factor is the number of hours worked for the employer within the meaning of the FLSA, which is not limited by methods of recordkeeping or inaccurate compensation agreements.
Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA's principles may be used to determine whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: For an employee returning from or reemployed following USERRA-covered service, in determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave (subject to § 825.801(c) for airline flight crew employees).
unit_attributes.statement: An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service in determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave, adding those hours to any hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period to meet the hours of service requirement (referencing § 825.801(c) for airline flight crew employees).

unit_attributes.scope_text: In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, the employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including for employees who are exempt from FLSA's recordkeeping requirement under 29 CFR part 541.
unit_attributes.statement: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including employees exempt from FLSA's recordkeeping requirement, the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours, and must be able to clearly demonstrate (for example, regarding full-time teachers) that the employee did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim the employee is not eligible for FMLA leave (referencing § 825.801(d) for airline flight crew employees).

The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee is on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee may be on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement, and in that event, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after the employee meets the eligibility requirement would be FMLA leave.
